mewf.title: Middle East Water Forum (MEWF)
mewf.description: A regional platform for utilities, experts and partners to share technical knowledge, training and innovation for sustainable water security.
mewf.overview: MEWF is a regional platform that brings utilities, policymakers and technical partners together around water security. GII supports the programme with German engineering expertise, training formats and applied innovation for sustainable water systems.
mewf.challenge: Water utilities and public institutions across the region often work in isolation, with limited access to applied engineering knowledge, structured training and practical innovation that can strengthen long-term water security.
mewf.solution: GII helped shape MEWF as a working forum for technical exchange, capacity building and applied water innovation, connecting regional partners with German expertise in sustainable water systems, training and programme design.
keyAreas: Water resources management and water security
Climate change and sustainable water management

clivent.title: CLIVENT
clivent.description: Energy-efficient ventilation and climate technology, connecting German environmental engineering with smarter building operations.
clivent.overview: CLIVENT develops energy-efficient ventilation and HVAC technology for buildings that need reliable climate control with lower energy demand. The project connects German environmental engineering with smarter operations for commercial and industrial facilities.
clivent.challenge: Commercial and industrial buildings need stable indoor climate, but conventional HVAC systems often use too much energy and are difficult to operate efficiently over time.
clivent.solution: GII connected German environmental engineering with smarter building operations through energy-efficient ventilation and HVAC technology designed to lower energy demand without weakening climate performance.

germanCare.title: German Care
germanCare.description: Medical technology and hospital-planning support for connected healthcare delivery, equipment and local supply.
germanCare.overview: German Care is an e-commerce and supply platform for medical technology, hospital planning and connected healthcare delivery. GII supports product access, equipment coordination and local supply so providers can source German-standard solutions more easily.
germanCare.challenge: Healthcare providers need reliable access to medical technology, hospital-planning support and local supply, but sourcing German-standard solutions is often fragmented across products, partners and logistics.
germanCare.solution: GII supports German Care as a digital commerce and supply platform that coordinates product access, medical equipment and hospital-planning support, making German-standard healthcare solutions easier to source and deliver.

urbanFeeding.title: Smart Urban Feeding & Water Station
urbanFeeding.description: IoT and wireless sensor networks for a smart feeding and water station in urban environments, developed for OneNex.
urbanFeeding.overview: GII contributed to a smart feeding and water station for urban environments, developed for OneNex. The system combines automated service functions with intelligent monitoring and connectivity, applying wireless sensor networks and IoT to link sensors, monitoring components and control functions in smart urban infrastructure.
urbanFeeding.challenge: Urban feeding and water infrastructure often lacks connected monitoring, so operators cannot reliably track food and water availability, consumption, operating status or environmental conditions in public space.
urbanFeeding.solution: GII applied IoT and WSN technologies to connect sensors, monitoring and control in one architecture, creating a foundation for remote monitoring and data-driven resource management that can be adapted to smart-city, environmental and public-space applications.

waterNetworkMonitoring.title: Utility Water Network Monitoring
waterNetworkMonitoring.description: IoT-based monitoring for distribution networks — flow, pressure and quality data that helps utilities detect issues before they reach customers.
waterNetworkMonitoring.overview: GII supports water utilities with connected monitoring for distribution networks, combining flow, pressure and quality sensors with dashboards operators can use during daily shifts. The approach focuses on practical leak detection, network visibility and alert paths maintenance teams can act on.
waterNetworkMonitoring.challenge: Water utilities often lack real-time visibility across distribution networks, so leaks, pressure drops and quality issues are discovered late — after customer complaints or costly losses.
waterNetworkMonitoring.solution: GII designs IoT monitoring architectures that connect field sensors, edge gateways and operator dashboards, giving utilities early signals on network performance with documentation and handover criteria field teams can support.

buildingEnergyMonitoring.title: Building Energy Monitoring Platform
buildingEnergyMonitoring.description: Cloud-based energy monitoring for commercial and public buildings — consumption visibility, alerts and reporting that help operators reduce cost without losing reliability.
buildingEnergyMonitoring.overview: GII builds building energy monitoring platforms that combine smart metering, dashboards and alert logic for facility teams. The focus is practical consumption visibility, baseline tracking and operating rules maintenance staff can support after handover.
buildingEnergyMonitoring.challenge: Facility teams often lack a single view of energy use across buildings, floors and systems, so inefficiency is discovered late and savings are hard to verify after upgrades.
buildingEnergyMonitoring.solution: GII delivers cloud-based monitoring with smart metering integration, role-based dashboards and documented alert thresholds, giving operators the visibility to act on consumption patterns in daily work.

hvacOperationsMonitoring.title: HVAC Operations Monitoring
hvacOperationsMonitoring.description: Monitoring and alert paths for ventilation and climate systems — indoor air quality, equipment status and energy performance facility teams can act on.
hvacOperationsMonitoring.overview: GII supports facility teams with HVAC operations monitoring that connects ventilation assets, climate controls and performance indicators in one operator view. The focus is practical indoor climate, equipment visibility and alert logic maintenance staff can support.
hvacOperationsMonitoring.challenge: Commercial buildings run complex ventilation and HVAC systems, but operators often lack unified visibility into air quality, equipment status and whether designed efficiency is maintained after commissioning.
hvacOperationsMonitoring.solution: GII delivers monitoring dashboards and alert paths mapped to daily facility work, with documented thresholds, training and handover criteria so climate performance stays reliable over time.

environmentalMonitoringNetwork.title: Environmental Monitoring Network
environmentalMonitoringNetwork.description: Sensor-based monitoring for air, resource use and environmental conditions — connected infrastructure teams can operate in public space and smart-city settings.
environmentalMonitoringNetwork.overview: GII supports environmental monitoring networks that connect field sensors, edge gateways and operator dashboards for teams managing public infrastructure, utilities and smart-city applications. The focus is practical visibility into environmental conditions and resource use operators can act on.
environmentalMonitoringNetwork.challenge: Public infrastructure and smart-city programmes often deploy sensors in isolation, so environmental data stays fragmented and teams cannot respond quickly to changing conditions or resource pressure.
environmentalMonitoringNetwork.solution: GII designs monitoring architectures that link sensors, communications and dashboards in one maintainable system, with documented alert paths and handover criteria field teams can support.

digitalLearningPlatform.title: Digital Learning Platform
digitalLearningPlatform.description: A bilingual learning and training platform for professional programmes — courses, workshops and knowledge resources educators and learners can use across regions.
digitalLearningPlatform.overview: GII supports digital learning platforms that combine course delivery, training workflows and knowledge resources for professional and capacity-building programmes. The focus is practical access for educators and learners, with administration paths programme teams can sustain.
digitalLearningPlatform.challenge: Training programmes often rely on fragmented documents, in-person sessions and email coordination, making it hard to scale learning, track progress or support learners across regions and languages.
digitalLearningPlatform.solution: GII delivers a structured learning platform with course modules, training paths, bilingual content support and admin reporting, giving programme teams a digital foundation they can extend as cohorts grow.

digitalCommerceMarketplace.title: Digital Commerce Marketplace
digitalCommerceMarketplace.description: A B2B ordering portal with product catalogues, account pricing and order tracking — built for specialist suppliers and procurement teams.
digitalCommerceMarketplace.overview: GII supports digital commerce marketplaces that connect specialist product catalogues with B2B ordering, account management and fulfillment visibility. The focus is practical buying for customers and manageable catalogues for operations teams.
digitalCommerceMarketplace.challenge: Specialist suppliers often manage orders through phone, email and static PDF catalogues, making it hard for buyers to compare products, track status or scale ordering across accounts and regions.
digitalCommerceMarketplace.solution: GII delivers a structured commerce portal with searchable catalogues, account-based ordering and admin tools, giving sales and operations teams a digital channel they can extend as product ranges grow.

enerbe.title: ENERBE – Smart Energy Monitoring & ICT Platform
enerbe.description: An EU-funded ICT platform and building energy monitoring system for public buildings, combining smart metering, cloud monitoring and energy efficiency.
enerbe.overview: GII implemented an ICT-driven smart energy monitoring project for public buildings in the Middle East within the EU-funded ENERBE initiative — Energy Efficiency through ICT-driven Behavioural Change in Public Buildings. As the contracted technology partner, GII provided technical assistance for a cloud-based Building Energy Monitoring System.
enerbe.challenge: Public buildings need to cut energy use through behavioural change, but consumption data is often fragmented and difficult to collect, monitor or manage through a single digital platform.
enerbe.solution: GII designed and developed a cloud-based ICT platform with smart metering, remote monitoring and control, multilevel administration and a scalable architecture, so energy-related information across public buildings can be collected, monitored and managed centrally.

svAkafa.title: Automotive Inspection & Digital Infrastructure
svAkafa.description: ICT systems integration and digital process optimization for a vehicle inspection facility, including ASA interfaces, networks and online appointment management.
svAkafa.overview: GII supported the digital and technical modernization of KFZ-Sachverständigenbüro SV-Akafa, a vehicle inspection facility in Germany. The work focused on integrating, stabilizing and optimizing ICT infrastructure and digital workflows across internal inspection systems and customer-facing services.
svAkafa.challenge: Vehicle inspection operations depend on reliable data transfer, network hardware and digital customer services, but specialized inspection systems and everyday ICT often sit apart and are difficult to keep in sync.
svAkafa.solution: GII optimized data communication through ASA interfaces, configured network and hardware, maintained inspection software, and supported website performance plus an online appointment solution synchronized with Outlook and Google — with ongoing technical support for digital inspection processes.

nexaOps.title: NexaOps Enterprise Platform
nexaOps.description: A connected operations platform that unifies workflows, reporting and supplier coordination for a multi-site manufacturer.
nexaOps.overview: GII helped a German manufacturer replace fragmented spreadsheets and legacy tools with NexaOps — a digital operations platform that connects production planning, service teams and management reporting in one place.
nexaOps.challenge: Operations ran across multiple sites with disconnected systems, making it hard to track orders, service cases and performance in real time.
nexaOps.solution: GII designed and delivered a modular platform with role-based dashboards, workflow automation and ERP integrations that teams could adopt step by step.

mittelstandCloud.title: Mittelstand Cloud Modernization
mittelstandCloud.description: Secure cloud migration and infrastructure modernization for a mid-sized enterprise moving off legacy on-premise systems.
mittelstandCloud.overview: GII supported a Mittelstand company through a phased cloud migration — modernizing infrastructure, securing data access and keeping business-critical applications available throughout the transition.
mittelstandCloud.challenge: Legacy servers, manual backups and limited remote access slowed growth and made it difficult to roll out new digital services safely.
mittelstandCloud.solution: GII planned and executed a staged migration with identity management, monitored workloads and clear rollback paths so teams could move to the cloud without disrupting daily operations.

publicServiceHub.title: Public Service Digital Hub
publicServiceHub.description: A citizen-facing digital hub for appointments, service requests and multilingual information across municipal departments.
publicServiceHub.overview: GII delivered a public service digital hub that lets citizens book appointments, submit requests and access department information online — reducing phone load and improving response times for municipal staff.
publicServiceHub.challenge: Citizens had to navigate multiple channels and paper forms, while staff spent significant time on repetitive enquiries and manual scheduling.
publicServiceHub.solution: GII built a unified portal with multilingual content, online forms, appointment booking and admin tools that integrated with existing department workflows.

smeProcurementHub.title: Mittelstand Procurement Hub
smeProcurementHub.description: A right-sized e-procurement portal that digitized supplier orders, approvals and stock visibility for a family-owned manufacturer.
smeProcurementHub.overview: GII helped a mid-sized manufacturer replace email-based ordering and spreadsheet stock lists with a procurement hub that purchasing, warehouse and management teams could run without a large IT department.
smeProcurementHub.challenge: Purchase requests moved through inboxes and phone calls, making it hard to track approvals, compare suppliers or see what was already on order.
smeProcurementHub.solution: GII delivered a phased portal with supplier catalogs, approval workflows and inventory snapshots integrated into existing ERP processes.

smeProductionPilot.title: Production Line Connectivity Pilot
smeProductionPilot.description: Machine status and quality data connected on an existing production line — without replacing equipment or stopping shifts.
smeProductionPilot.overview: GII ran a focused Industry 4.0 pilot for a Mittelstand manufacturer, adding connectivity to one bottleneck line so operators and shift leads could see downtime and quality events in real time.
smeProductionPilot.challenge: Production issues were reported verbally at shift handover, with no reliable view of machine status or recurring quality defects during the run.
smeProductionPilot.solution: GII connected selected machines, built operator-facing dashboards and trained shift leads to act on alerts — proving value before expanding to other lines.

smeFieldServiceApp.title: Dealer Field Service App
smeFieldServiceApp.description: A mobile service app for technicians and dealers to log visits, parts and customer cases from the field.
smeFieldServiceApp.overview: GII digitized after-sales service for a Mittelstand equipment supplier — giving technicians a mobile app for job sheets, spare parts requests and customer history while keeping admin workflows simple.
smeFieldServiceApp.challenge: Service teams relied on paper job sheets and late office data entry, delaying invoicing and making it difficult to see open cases across dealers.
smeFieldServiceApp.solution: GII built a mobile-first field service app with offline-friendly job capture, parts lookup and a lightweight back-office view for coordinators.

industry40OeeDashboard.title: Shop-Floor OEE Dashboard
industry40OeeDashboard.description: Real-time OEE, downtime and shift reporting for operators and production leads on a connected assembly line.
industry40OeeDashboard.overview: GII connected machine signals from an existing assembly line and delivered operator-facing OEE dashboards — giving shift leads a live view of availability, performance and quality without replacing equipment.
industry40OeeDashboard.challenge: Downtime was tracked manually at shift handover, with no shared view of which machines were running, idle or waiting on maintenance.
industry40OeeDashboard.solution: GII integrated machine data, built shift dashboards and trained production leads to use alerts during the run — starting with one line before expanding plant-wide.

industry40PredictiveMaintenance.title: Predictive Maintenance Pilot
industry40PredictiveMaintenance.description: Sensor-based condition monitoring on critical assets to reduce unplanned downtime on a manufacturing plant floor.
industry40PredictiveMaintenance.overview: GII ran a predictive maintenance pilot for a manufacturer — monitoring vibration and temperature on selected assets and routing alerts to maintenance teams before failures stopped production.
industry40PredictiveMaintenance.challenge: Maintenance was largely reactive, with breakdowns causing unplanned stops and limited data on which assets were degrading.
industry40PredictiveMaintenance.solution: GII installed sensors, defined alert thresholds and connected maintenance workflows so technicians could act on warnings during planned windows.

industry40QualityTraceability.title: Digital Quality Traceability
industry40QualityTraceability.description: Lot-level quality logging and traceability across production steps for a precision parts manufacturer.
industry40QualityTraceability.overview: GII digitized quality checks and lot traceability for a precision manufacturer — replacing paper logs with digital capture at key production steps and searchable history for quality teams.
industry40QualityTraceability.challenge: Quality records lived in paper binders, making it slow to trace defects back to a batch, machine or operator shift.
industry40QualityTraceability.solution: GII built digital quality forms, barcode-linked lot tracking and reporting views that quality and production teams could use without disrupting the line.

iotUtilityMonitoring.title: Utility IoT Monitoring Network
iotUtilityMonitoring.description: Wireless sensor network for flow, pressure and asset monitoring across a utility distribution network.
iotUtilityMonitoring.overview: GII deployed an IoT monitoring network for a utility operator — connecting field sensors, edge gateways and operator dashboards so teams could see network status and respond to alerts during daily operations.
iotUtilityMonitoring.challenge: Sensor data sat in separate systems or never reached the teams on shift, making it hard to verify leaks, pressure events or asset faults quickly.
iotUtilityMonitoring.solution: GII integrated sensors, communications and monitoring views mapped to operator actions — with documentation and training so utility teams could maintain the network.

iotIndustrialEdgeGateway.title: Industrial Edge Gateway Rollout
iotIndustrialEdgeGateway.description: Edge gateways that collect machine and sensor data on the plant floor for dashboards and integration platforms.
iotIndustrialEdgeGateway.overview: GII rolled out industrial edge gateways for a manufacturer — collecting machine signals at the line, buffering data locally and forwarding structured events to monitoring and integration systems.
iotIndustrialEdgeGateway.challenge: Production data was trapped at machines or required manual exports, with no reliable path from the shop floor to the systems teams used for reporting.
iotIndustrialEdgeGateway.solution: GII specified edge hardware, connectivity and data models, then deployed gateways with clear handover criteria for plant IT and maintenance teams.

medicalDeviceMonitoring.title: Medical Device Monitoring Platform
medicalDeviceMonitoring.description: Connected monitoring for medical devices with alert routing, status dashboards and maintenance workflows for clinical teams.
medicalDeviceMonitoring.overview: GII built a medical device monitoring platform that connects equipment status, alerts and maintenance workflows — giving clinical and technical teams shared visibility without replacing existing hospital systems.
medicalDeviceMonitoring.challenge: Device status and maintenance alerts were scattered across vendor tools, making it hard for clinical and technical teams to respond consistently during daily operations.
medicalDeviceMonitoring.solution: GII integrated device signals, monitoring views and alert paths mapped to the roles that act on them — with documentation and training for sustainable hospital operation.

hospitalPlanningPlatform.title: Hospital Planning Digital Platform
hospitalPlanningPlatform.description: Digital platform for hospital planning, equipment coordination and connected care delivery workflows.
hospitalPlanningPlatform.overview: GII supported a hospital planning platform that coordinates equipment requirements, planning workflows and connected care delivery — helping providers manage complex healthcare projects in one digital environment.
hospitalPlanningPlatform.challenge: Hospital planning involved fragmented spreadsheets, email threads and supplier coordination, slowing equipment decisions and connected care rollout.
hospitalPlanningPlatform.solution: GII shaped a digital planning platform with structured workflows, equipment coordination and handover documentation so clinical, planning and supply teams could work from shared information.

cloudSecurityOperations.title: Cloud Security Operations Platform
cloudSecurityOperations.description: Monitoring, access control and security operations for cloud workloads supporting business-critical applications.
cloudSecurityOperations.overview: GII built a cloud security operations platform that centralizes monitoring, access policies and incident workflows — giving IT teams shared visibility across workloads without replacing existing business applications.
cloudSecurityOperations.challenge: Cloud environments grew faster than security practices, leaving inconsistent access control, unclear monitoring and reactive incident handling across critical workloads.
cloudSecurityOperations.solution: GII integrated monitoring views, role-based access and operating procedures mapped to the teams that maintain cloud services — with documentation and training for sustainable security operations.

aiOperationsAssistant.title: AI Operations Assistant
aiOperationsAssistant.description: An AI assistant embedded in daily operations workflows to route tasks, summarize cases and support service teams.
aiOperationsAssistant.overview: GII delivered an AI operations assistant for a multi-site organization — helping service teams summarize cases, route work and find answers inside the platform they already used for daily operations.
aiOperationsAssistant.challenge: Operations teams spent too much time searching records, writing summaries and manually routing cases across disconnected tools.
aiOperationsAssistant.solution: GII integrated an assistant into existing workflows with role-based access, audit-friendly outputs and human review paths so teams could adopt AI support step by step.

aiQualityAnalytics.title: AI Quality Analytics Pilot
aiQualityAnalytics.description: A pilot analytics layer that flags quality patterns and supports production teams with faster insight from shop-floor data.
aiQualityAnalytics.overview: GII built an AI quality analytics pilot for a manufacturer — surfacing patterns in production and quality data so teams could investigate issues faster without replacing existing MES workflows.
aiQualityAnalytics.challenge: Quality data existed but sat in reports teams reviewed too late, making it hard to connect recurring defects to line conditions or process steps.
aiQualityAnalytics.solution: GII connected structured production signals with an analytics layer and review workflows mapped to quality and shift leads, with clear handover criteria before wider rollout.

aiKnowledgeAssistant.title: AI Knowledge Assistant
aiKnowledgeAssistant.description: A secure knowledge assistant that helps teams query manuals, policies and project history inside their operational platform.
aiKnowledgeAssistant.overview: GII delivered an AI knowledge assistant for an organization with scattered documentation — enabling teams to search institutional knowledge, summarize answers and cite sources without leaving the tools they already use.
aiKnowledgeAssistant.challenge: Critical knowledge lived across PDFs, wikis and email threads, making it slow for staff to find reliable answers during customer and project work.
aiKnowledgeAssistant.solution: GII indexed approved content sources, built a role-aware assistant with source citations and integrated it into the existing operations platform with audit-friendly access rules.

aiDocumentProcessing.title: AI Document Processing
aiDocumentProcessing.description: Automated classification and data extraction for inbound documents, forms and supplier records.
aiDocumentProcessing.overview: GII implemented an AI document processing pipeline for a back-office team — classifying incoming files, extracting key fields and routing results into existing review workflows.
aiDocumentProcessing.challenge: Staff manually opened, sorted and re-keyed information from large volumes of PDFs and scanned forms, creating delays and inconsistent data entry.
aiDocumentProcessing.solution: GII built a document intake flow with AI classification and extraction, human review for exceptions and direct handoff to downstream systems teams already maintained.

mittelstandRoadmap.title: A practical digitalization roadmap for the Mittelstand
mittelstandRoadmap.excerpt: How mid-sized companies move from a digital maturity check to a sequence of systems they can actually run.
body: Many mid-sized companies already know they need to digitalize. The harder question is where to start, which processes to touch first, and how to avoid buying software that operators cannot run six months later.

GII treats the roadmap as a delivery sequence, not a slide deck. We begin with a digital maturity check, map the operating model, then specify the first systems that reduce manual work without forcing a full IT replacement. Each step has an owner, a training path and a way to measure whether the process is actually in use.

The result is a plan that fits German Mittelstand conditions: existing machinery, limited IT teams, and the need to keep production running while new tools are introduced. Strategy only counts when the next system is live.

iotWaterUtilities.title: What IoT monitoring changes for water utilities
iotWaterUtilities.excerpt: Sensors only help if operators can see, trust and act on the data in daily operations.
body: Water utilities collect more sensor data than they can often use. Flow, pressure, quality and asset status sit in separate systems, or they reach a dashboard that nobody checks during a night shift.

IoT and wireless sensor networks change that only when monitoring is designed around operations. GII connects sensors, communications and control so operators get a clear picture of what is happening in the network, and so alerts map to actions they already know how to take.
The value is not the device count. It is leak detection that can be verified, quality events that can be traced, and a monitoring architecture that utilities can maintain with their own teams.

industry40Smes.title: Industry 4.0 without a factory reset
industry40Smes.excerpt: How smaller manufacturers add connectivity and data to existing lines instead of replacing them.
body: Industry 4.0 programmes often assume a greenfield plant. Most manufacturers GII works with have lines that still earn money, skilled operators, and no appetite for a factory reset.

The practical path is to add connectivity where it improves a known bottleneck: machine status, quality checks, energy use or maintenance. Data then has to reach the people who run the shift, not only a central analytics team.
German engineering standards still apply. Interfaces, documentation and training decide whether a connected line stays connected after the project team leaves.

hvacEnergy.title: Lower energy use without losing indoor climate
hvacEnergy.excerpt: A look at how energy-efficient ventilation can be specified, commissioned and operated in commercial buildings.
body: Commercial and industrial buildings need stable indoor climate, but conventional HVAC systems often use more energy than the operation can justify. Cutting consumption only works if comfort, air quality and reliability stay intact.

This case looks at energy-efficient ventilation specified for day-to-day operations rather than a one-off efficiency claim. Commissioning, operator training and monitoring decide whether the designed savings appear in the energy bill.
GII’s work in this area connects German environmental engineering with building operations: the technology has to be installable, tunable and understandable for the facilities team that inherits it.

germanTechMena.title: Connecting German technology with MENA programmes
germanTechMena.excerpt: What international partners need when German engineering has to be delivered, trained and maintained across borders.
body: German technology has a strong reputation in water, energy, medical systems and industrial software. International programmes still fail when equipment arrives without training, spare parts, bilingual documentation or a partner who stays after handover.

This paper sets out how GII structures that transfer: German engineering standards, Arabic and English delivery where needed, and a path from specification to operation. The goal is technology that local teams can run, not a catalogue of products left unused.
Public institutions and development partners need that operating layer as much as the hardware. Partnerships work when roles for training, maintenance and knowledge exchange are defined at the start.

mewfForumRecap.title: Notes from the Middle East Water Forum
mewfForumRecap.excerpt: Themes from regional exchange on water security, training and applied German water technology.
body: The Middle East Water Forum brings utilities, policymakers and technical partners together around water security. GII’s role is to keep the exchange practical: applied water systems, training formats and German engineering that can be used in regional conditions.

Recurring themes this year included bilingual knowledge platforms, the water-energy-food-environment nexus, and the shortage of structured capacity building for utility staff. Technology without operators remains a short-lived investment.
MEWF continues as a working forum rather than a one-off conference. The value is the network of utilities and experts who can share methods, not only presentations.

publicDigitalPlatforms.title: Webinar: Digital platforms for public institutions
publicDigitalPlatforms.excerpt: A session on portals, knowledge libraries and bilingual platforms that public teams can administer.
body: Public institutions need platforms that connect people, documents, events and services without becoming another system only a vendor can change. This webinar walks through the modules GII specifies most often: directories, knowledge libraries, multilingual content and role-based administration.

The session is aimed at programme leads and IT counterparts who have to keep a platform alive after launch. We cover what belongs in the first release, what can wait, and how Arabic/English delivery changes information architecture.
Recordings and notes are shared with registered participants. If you are planning a portal or knowledge platform, the same questions can be taken into a project conversation with GII.

smartUrbanInfra.title: Smart urban infrastructure: a field report
smartUrbanInfra.excerpt: Lessons from connecting sensors, feeding stations and water points in public space.
body: Smart-city projects often start with a dashboard. In the field, the first problem is usually simpler: whether a feeding or water station has supply, whether a sensor is still transmitting, and who is responsible when it is not.

This report draws on GII’s work with IoT and wireless sensor networks for urban feeding and water infrastructure. Connectivity, monitoring and control have to sit in one architecture that operators can service in public space.
The lesson is scale through operations, not through more devices. A station that reports reliably and can be maintained locally is more useful than a network that looks complete on a map.
